newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close lower on weather, fund selling.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close lower on weather, fund selling.

text.p: Good crop weather in the U.S. Midwest and forecasts for nearly ideal weather to continue knocked CBOT soybean futures to a lower close, traders said.
Fund selling again was featured and totaled at least 35.0 million bushels, they said.

"There was huge fund selling, a bearish six- to 10-day and follow through from yesterday," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds. Monday's National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook was for above to much above normal temperatures and normal to no precipitation in the U.S. Midwest from October 6 through October 10.
Also, USDA Monday said during the week ended Sunday the U.S. soybean crop condition improved to 57 percent good to excellent, up from 55 percent the previous week.
"It's continued fund liquidation. The crop conditions improved and the six- to 10-day certainly wasn't friendly," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
The fund selling was led by Merrill Lynch Futures with at least 25.0 million bushels sold in the November contract, the traders said.
Soybeans closed four to 10-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with November down 8-3/4 cents at $7.49-1/4.
Traders said Refco Inc, Griffin Trading and Iowa Grain each sold from three to five million bushels of November.
November touched a session low of $7.44 per bushel, a two-month low and the lowest level for that contract since $7.43 was reached on August 8.

Soybeans attempted to recover late on a firm tone in soyoil and on attempts at bargain buying. The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for November ended the day at 23.824 points, a signal that contract may be viewed as oversold.
An RSI of 20 or less generally is considered an oversold signal and 80 or more overbought. The 14-day RSI for November ended at 32.987.
The four-day moving average for November ended at $7.70-3/8, 14-day at $7.92 and 40-day at $7.85-1/8.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 80,000 contracts, down from 88,180 Monday, according to the CBOT.

In soybean options, Smith Barney bought 1,500 May $7.50 calls and sold 1,500 May $7.75 puts at 15 cents, Cargill Investor Services bought 1,000 March $7.25 puts at 13 cents, USA Trading bought 1,000 January $8.25 calls and sold 1,000 January $8.50 calls at 2-1/2 cents, the traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 32,000 contracts, down from 46,608 Monday.
